Q: Python modules from .pth files overwrites editable install A:

Thanks for the comments and apologies if the question lacked details!

I found the answer in the way that - in my case - setuptools creates editable installs and provides them to the import mechanic:

It creates an EditableFinder, which is then appended to sys.meta_path. This way, editable packages will always be shadowed by anything with the same name that can be found using the PathFinder which searches sys.path and is per default called before any EditableFinder.

Since I find this behavior slightly unintuitive, I proposed to change it here.

Q: How do I detect whether a variable is a function? A:

The result of type of any function is the same object, or at least comparable

  # define a variable typeFunction using any function
  typeFunction = type(lambda x: 1)

  def a():
     pass

  type(a) == typeFunction

or directly

  type(a) == type (lambda x: 1)

also it can be done as a function

def isFunction (object, _comptype = type (lambda x: 1))
    return type(object) == _comptype

isFunction (a)

Q: Where to add the response type of a Api call inside a custom base Query in RTK query? A:

Maybe you are overcomplicating things? I don't know your Typescript types/interfaces nor what your endpoints actually return, but I'd hazard a guess that you probably will cast refreshResult (currently typed unknown by default) to RefreshTokenResponse, i.e. the direct response value type, i.e. not wrapped in some generic API type wrapper the RTKQ endpoints use.

FWIW it doesn't appear this is a actually a question about general "best practices" and is actually a very specific question about a specific programming problem you are trying to solve. It probably ought to have been posts as a regular Q-and-A post instead of a subjective discussions post that doesn't really receive attention nor a specific answer.
